We need teach student with demonstration pairs. Need understand rule. Input: background color at (0,0). There is upright stripe (full height) of one color, and flat stripe (full width) of another color. They intersect. In input, at crossing, one color is shown on top (upright stripe maybe over flat). Output: swap crossing so the other stripe is on top. Essentially at crossing rectangle, set to opposite color.

Verifier details: back = grid[0][0]. upright columns = columns in row 0 where != back (the vertical stripe columns). flat rows = rows in col 0 where != back (horizontal stripe rows). up_colour = color of vertical stripe at row0. flat_colour = color of horizontal at col0. For each intersection (r in flat, c in upright), set out[r][c] = flat_colour if grid[r][c] == up_colour else up_colour. Since at crossing in input all cells are one of the colors? Actually input at crossing: the top stripe color covers crossing. If upright on top, crossing = up_colour; output becomes flat_colour. If flat on top, crossing = flat_colour; output becomes up_colour. So it swaps crossing to other color. Wait if grid[r][c] is up_colour -> flat; else (flat) -> up. So always toggles to other color.

Need produce demonstrations. Student sees pairs input/output only. Need enough to infer rule. We can choose inputs that verifier can evaluate. Need combinations showing both directions? The rule says change color where lines meet so other line on top. We should show examples covering different colors, orientations, stripe widths, maybe both crossing orders.

Important: input grid rectangular. The stripes: vertical stripe(s) (full height) and horizontal stripe(s) (full width). Neither touches edge? Actually rule says neither touches edge, first row shows upright alone and first column flat alone. So background at corner. Vertical stripe columns are in row0 != back. Horizontal stripe rows in col0 != back. They don't include row0 or col0? The upright stripe can include columns possibly not edge. Flat rows not edge. Intersection exists.

Need ensure verifier can evaluate. It doesn't require stripe not touching edge? It uses row0 and col0. If vertical stripe includes column 0? Then grid[0][0] would be up color? back = grid[0][0] so then upright would exclude? Could mess. So we keep background at (0,0), vertical stripe not column 0, horizontal not row 0. Also background color can be any, stripes any two distinct colors. Thickness can vary.

We want teach. We can provide several pairs. Need choose inputs maybe handcrafted to show mapping. Since student infers from pairs. We should probably include clear examples: horizontal stripe of color A crosses vertical stripe of color B, where crossing currently B (vertical on top), output crossing becomes A. And another where crossing currently A, output becomes B. Also maybe different background colors. Also different widths.

Need ensure verifier's logic: back = grid[0][0]. upright = [c for c in range(w) if grid[0][c] != back]. flat = [r for r in range(h) if grid[r][0] != back]. If vertical stripe color != horizontal color. Then for each flat row and upright col, set out[r][c] = flat_colour if grid[r][c] == up_colour else up_colour. This toggles.
